{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-az-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"53d06377b134a52ef973779baf95eef83b24a92434e62e3b1e3015a5a392c85f","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-az-class-d:lineage:10","source_registry_sha256":"6dbbc2d22fea619728bdb90038a4aedf3afc07eab652b3f97027c9c69aaadaf4","source_liveness_sha256":"1c5753487760cbe2044d84b5696121c7181af61815b598d89d5ce158abf5fe43"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"License classes, instruction permits and the graduated license","heading":"C — License classes, instruction permits, graduated license restrictions and penalties, parent or guardian approval, Selective Service and the Class D operator license","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — License classes, instruction permits, graduated license restrictions and penalties, parent or guardian approval, Selective Service and the Class D operator license
Knowledge domain: how Arizona sorts licenses into classes, who may get which instruction permit and how it must be supervised, what a teen graduated license allows and forbids in its first months, the penalties for young drivers, who must sign for a minor, and what the Class D operator license covers.

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
Your Social Security number is used to verify your identity and to comply with child support laws, and it is not used as your driver license number. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
Arizona issues licenses by class: Class G for graduated, Class D for operator, Class M for motorcycle, and Classes A, B and C for commercial drivers. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
When a Class M license is combined with another class, the motorcycle privilege is added as an endorsement on the back of the current license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A01
You may get a graduated and/or motorcycle instruction permit once you are at least 15 years and 6 months old, but an operator permit requires age 18. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A01
A graduated or operator permit holder must drive with a Class A, B, C or D licensed driver who is at least 21 and sits in the seat beside them. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A01
Graduated and operator instruction permits are valid for 12 months. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A01
A motorcycle permit holder may not carry passengers, may not ride on freeways or interstate highways, and may not ride between sunset and sunrise or whenever light is too poor to see people or vehicles 500 feet away. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A01
A motorcycle permit is valid for 7 months and can be renewed only once within a 24-month period. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A01
MVD offers practice for the written test on its website, azdot.gov/mvd. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A01
A graduated license goes to applicants who are at least 16 but under 18 and lets them drive any vehicle that needs no motorcycle or commercial license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A01
During the first 6 months, a graduated license holder must stay off the road from midnight to 5:00 a.m., except when the front passenger seat is occupied by a parent or legal guardian holding a valid Class A, B, C or D license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A01
The night limit also does not apply when the teen is driving directly to or from a sanctioned school-sponsored activity, a job, a sanctioned religious activity or a family emergency. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A01
During the first 6 months, a graduated license holder may not drive with more than one passenger under age 18, unless those passengers are the teen's siblings or a licensed parent or legal guardian rides in the front passenger seat. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A02
You must pass the Division written test before MVD will issue an Arizona instruction permit, though this rule does not cover Commercial Learner's Permits. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A02
Arizona credits applicants for the time they held an instruction permit in another state. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A02
To get a graduated license you must have held an Arizona instruction permit for at least 6 months, and the permit must still be valid when you apply. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A02
A graduated-license applicant must also finish an MVD-approved Arizona driver education program, or a parent or guardian must certify the required supervised practice in writing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A02
The certified practice is at least 30 hours of supervised driving with at least 10 at night, or 20 hours with at least 6 at night when the minor completed a Traffic Survival School or Defensive Driving course. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A02
Someone already holding a current and valid license from another state may be excused from the permit, driver education and practice-hour requirements. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A02
A graduated license holder does not have to switch to an operator license at age 18 but may choose to. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A02
If you get a citation you may be eligible for the Arizona Supreme Court's Defensive Driving Program, so read the information that comes with the citation carefully. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A02
For a driver under 18 with a graduated license, a first traffic-violation conviction means mandatory Traffic Survival School and the violation goes on the driving record. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A02
A second conviction brings a 3-month suspension of the driving privilege, and a third brings a 6-month suspension, each also recorded on the driving record. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A02
Breaking the curfew or passenger restrictions brings extra penalties, including fines and a mandatory extension of the 6-month restricted period. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A02
A third conviction for curfew or passenger violations results in suspension, and so do convictions for other violations, including alcohol-related ones. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A02
If you are under 18, at least one adult must sign your instruction permit or driver license application. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A03
The adult who signs for a minor becomes responsible for any negligence or willful misconduct while the minor drives. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A03
The signer is one natural or adoptive parent when the parents are married to each other, both parents when unmarried with joint custody, or the one parent with sole custody. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec03-F29 | anchor: A03
Other permitted signers are a legal guardian or a foster parent living with the minor (each with proof), or the minor's employer if the parents' death certificates are shown. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec03-F30 | anchor: A03
The signatures must be witnessed by an MVD agent or a notary public, and signatures given for the instruction permit must be given again for the driver license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec03-F31 | anchor: A03
The person who signed for the minor, or the person responsible for the minor, may cancel the minor's license by submitting a Driver License/ID Cancellation Request or a notarized letter to MVD. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec03-F32 | anchor: A03
A cancellation request must state the license number, full name and date of birth of the person whose license is being canceled. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec03-F33 | anchor: A03
Federal law requires male United States citizens and male aliens living in the country to register with the Selective Service System within 30 days of turning 18. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec03-F34 | anchor: A03
By applying for an original, renewal or reinstatement license or ID, a male applicant under 26 consents to Selective Service registration, while for a duplicate the consent is optional. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec03-F35 | anchor: A03
Applicants aged 18 to 25 have their registration information sent to Selective Service immediately, while for those under 18 it is held and sent automatically at 18; registering does not mean joining the military. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec03-F36 | anchor: A04
A Class D operator license lets you drive any vehicle that does not require a motorcycle or commercial license, and you must be at least 18 to apply for one. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec03-F37 | anchor: A04
Riding a motorcycle or motor driven cycle requires a Class M license or endorsement, which you can apply for from age 16. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec03-F38 | anchor: A04
An under-18 motorcycle applicant needs at least six months holding an Arizona motorcycle permit, plus either an MVD-approved motorcycle course or a parent certifying 30 hours of supervised riding. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec03-F39 | anchor: A04
A commercial driver license in Class A, B or C is required for commercial motor vehicles, and its requirements are covered in the separate CDL manual rather than this one. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0015]

Misconceptions: a graduated-license teen is not banned from all passengers — siblings are allowed and one non-sibling passenger under eighteen is allowed; the night limit has exceptions for school, work, religious activities and family emergencies; turning eighteen does not force a graduated driver to get an operator license; the permit supervisor must sit beside the learner, not in the back seat.
Mnemonics: Fifteen-and-a-half to permit, sixteen to graduate, eighteen to operate; for the first six months of a graduated license, think One teen passenger and home by Midnight.
Glossary: Class G means the graduated license for drivers from sixteen up to eighteen; Class D means the operator license; endorsement means an added privilege printed on the back of a license, such as motorcycle; Traffic Survival School means the program for drivers with serious violations or points; notary public means an official who witnesses signatures.
Dynamic facts: the website for written-test practice and the cancellation request form location are service details that can change; the ages, hours and suspension lengths come from statute and change only by law.
